newsitem.title: UK: Vickers says confident after "useful" H1.
newsitem.headline: Vickers says confident after "useful" H1.

text.p: British auto and defence engineering group Vickers Plc said on Thursday that it was confident of being able to make further earnings progress in the second half of the year after it reported an 18 percent rise in first half pretax profit to 31.8 million pounds ($50 million).
"This performance, usefully ahead of the comparable period for last year, represents a process of consolidation during a period of investment for the future," Vickers said in its statement.

Sales rose by 11 percent across the group's divisions and included a strong performance by Rolls Royce Motor Cars, whose worldwide sales of Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars were up by 26 percent in the period compared with first half 1995.

However, Vickers said a combination of a continued high level of investment in production facilities, and what it called "a less rich mix" of top-line car sales that restrained margins, moderated Rolls Royce's performance.
Vickers also announced a series of top board changes, which will mean it has to hire a new chief executive and a new chief financial officer during the coming 18 months.

Chief executive Sir Colin Chandler will become first deputy chairman, as of today, and then chairman in April next year, retaining his chief executive's post for about another year thereafter. Finance chief Roger Head has asked to step down from the board at the end of December, after 10 years at his post.
